answer: Each agent must claim an exclusive mesa that alone produces fresh nectar via a memory-hard sequential hash chain; that nectar continuously reseeds the agent's private cipher so every subsequent proof depends on the unbroken mesa history. Because nectar is non-transferable and any attempt to fork the mesa invalidates prior nectar, an attacker needs a separate dedicated mesa and its full sequential nectar stream for each sybil identity, making the cost linear in the number of fakes and impossible to amortize across a botnet.
